summary.text: A 30-year-old woman 6 months post-partum, with a family history of lupus and sickle cell trait, had slowly worsening anxiety and depressive behaviors since childbirth per family and stopped breastfeeding the day before acute symptom onset. Reported features included rapid behavioral changes with tremors, rigidity, grimacing and hallucinations. An outside hospital diagnosed primary psychosis, but inpatient psychiatry rejected her for labile hypertension, and she was transferred to the authors hospital with subacute altered mental status.

She was tachycardic, hypertensive and catatonic with a BFCRS of 35. Labs showed leukocytosis and a positive cannabinoid screen. Chest CT suggested infectious bronchiolitis, head CT and MRI were unremarkable, cEEG showed diffuse disturbance without seizures, and CSF showed lymphocytic pleocytosis with negative infectious studies. Serum anti-neuronal autoantibodies were negative and CSF autoantibody studies could not be performed.

Lorazepam improved catatonia but needed escalation to 30 mg per 24 hours, with divalproex, IV methylprednisolone, IVIG and amantadine added. Lowering lorazepam failed with BFCRS up to 26, and ECT was not possible because she could not consent. After amantadine was increased she improved by hospital day 17, received rituximab, and moved to inpatient rehabilitation by hospital day 28.

By hospital day 31 she was alert with minor residual grimacing, amnesia and tinnitus, and her last BFCRS was 5. She was discharged home on amantadine, divalproex, carvedilol, vitamin D, lorazepam and prednisone tapers and prophylactic sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim with outpatient follow-up. The authors report complete recovery with a diagnosis of probable autoimmune encephalitis.
